Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra

forms, sounds, scents, tastes, tangible objects, and mental phenomena; this is what is called a <term>Srota-apanna</term> <gloss>stream-enterer</gloss>.

Subhūti, what do you think? Can a <term>Sakṛdāgāmin</term> <gloss>once-returner</gloss> have the thought, "I have attained the fruit of a <term>Sakṛdāgāmin</term>"? Subhūti replied, "No, World-Honored One. Why? Because a <term>Sakṛdāgāmin</term> is named 'once-returner,' but in reality, there is no coming or going; therefore, it is called <term>Sakṛdāgāmin</term>."

Subhūti, what do you think? Can an <term>Anāgāmin</term> <gloss>non-returner</gloss> have the thought, "I have attained the fruit of an <term>Anāgāmin</term>"? Subhūti replied, "No, World-Honored One. Why? Because an <term>Anāgāmin</term> is named 'non-returner,' but in reality, there is no 'not coming'; therefore, it is called <term>Anāgāmin</term>."

<summary>This page discusses the non-attainment nature of the stages of enlightenment, specifically the second and third fruits of the path, demonstrating that these titles are designations rather than states of being with actual motion or location.</summary>
